title: They Got Their Missing Boy Back… DNA Says It Wasn't Him
format: viral-short (45-75 s, one reveal, loop ending)
lines: In 1913, a family got their missing little boy back. Ninety years later, a DNA test proved he was never their son.
August 1912, Louisiana. Four year old Bobby Dunbar vanished on a family fishing trip at a swamp lake. For eight months, the whole country searched.
Then, in Mississippi, police found a boy traveling with a wandering handyman. The Dunbars said, that's our Bobby.
But a poor single mother from North Carolina came forward. Julia Anderson. She said, that's my son, Bruce.
Two mothers. One little boy. And a court had to choose.
The judge gave him to the Dunbars. The handyman was convicted of kidnapping. Julia went home alone.
The boy grew up as Bobby Dunbar. He married, had children, and died in 1966.
Then in 2004, his granddaughter asked for a DNA test. The result? He was not a Dunbar.
He was almost certainly Bruce Anderson. Which means the real Bobby Dunbar was never found.

structure.hook: line 0: family got their boy back, DNA 90 years later says it was never him (cold open, not whispered)
structure.5W1H: who (Bobby Dunbar, Julia Anderson, William Walters), what (disputed identity of a recovered child), when (Aug 1912, Apr 1913, 2004), where (Swayze Lake, Louisiana; Mississippi; North Carolina), how (court decision; Y-DNA test), why (two families claimed the same boy)
rehooks: line 4: two mothers, one boy, a court had to choose
structure.payoff: lines 7-8: not a Dunbar; the real Bobby was never found
structure.cta: on-screen FOLLOW button during line 8; loop ending ("never found" -> "In 1913, a family got their boy back")

notes: Sources: Wikipedia 'Disappearance of Bobby Dunbar'; NPR This American Life ep. 'The Ghosts of Bobby Dunbar' (2008); AP 2004 report on the DNA test. Bobby Dunbar (4) disappeared 23 Aug 1912 at Swayze Lake, Louisiana. Found ~8 months later (Apr 1913) in Mississippi with William Cantwell Walters, an itinerant handyman/piano tuner. Julia Anderson, unmarried, from North Carolina, said the boy was her son Bruce. Court awarded custody to the Dunbars; Walters convicted of kidnapping (conviction later overturned). The boy lived as Bobby Dunbar, had children, died 1966. 2004 Y-DNA comparison arranged after research by granddaughter Margaret Dunbar Cutright: no match to the Dunbar line; widely concluded he was Bruce Anderson. The real Bobby Dunbar's fate is unknown.
